messages:
cheng: Heads-up — noticed a pattern where mixed-dim embedding payloads trigger the rate limiter and we get a flurry of 413s + ambiguous error text. Curious if we should surface "suggested_split_plan" to clients and the console so SDKs can auto-split.

sam: Can you paste an example request and the exact error body?

cheng: Sure — short one: `POST /v1/embeddings` content-length ~1.2MB, body has 8 vectors at dims [512, 1024 mix]. Response is `413 Oversize: payload too large` with no hint. ops-bot attached the deploy log.

ops-bot: Deploy log: `rate_limiter:reject type=oversize reason=bytes_and_dim_mismatch tenant=acme corp route=embed-v1`

lucy: Ugh yeah. Right now runtime only returns generic 413. If we included a minimal suggestion like `{ "suggested_split_plan": [ {"count":4, "dims":512}, {"count":4, "dims":1024} ], "estimated_units": 240 }` clients could retry smartly.

maria: I like adding the hint. We need to think about telemetry/abuse vectors though — adding planning info might let noisy clients craft many retries. Suggest the header approach first: `X-Embed-Suggest-Split: base64(json)` so it's optional for SDKs to decode. Console can decode too.

sam: Header is fine. Also we should emit a `route_decision.reason` tag in traces (eg `split_hint_available`) and a counter metric `embed.suggested_splits_total`. That way console dashboards can show how often we provide split suggestions vs hard rejects.

tim: For rollout, propose opt-in via feature flag per-tenant. Start with 5% of traffic for small customers then expand. We should also add a `split_suggestion_sample_rate` field so we only compute plan for sampled requests (cheap).

lucy: Good call. Computing split plan is a little CPU work for huge payloads. We can do heuristics: if bytes>750KB or dims-mix detected, do a lightweight plan. Otherwise no-op.

maria: Console UX: add a new panel under Embeddings -> Preflight that shows "suggested split rate", "successful auto-retries", and a heatmap of `oversize_by_bytes` by tenant. Also link to sample request and split plan. Should be helpful during customer trouble-shooting.

cheng: One more API nuance — if SDK auto-splits we need to preserve ordering/idempotency. Suggest we return `split_plan_id` in the header so retries are traceable: `X-Split-Plan-ID: sp-<uuid>`. Telemetry should link requests to that id.

sam: Agree. We'll add a `split_plan.request_count` gauge and a `split_plan.retry_success_total` counter. Also record latency impact per split.

ops-bot: Note: security review — avoid leaking tenant quota heuristics in the body. Keep suggestions generic and scoped to the requesting tenant only.

lucy: SDK side: implement decode of header, do async split+bulk retry with exponential backoff. Add a flag `autoApplySplitHints: false` default. Docs should show examples.

maria: OK action items: 1) eng-runtime: add header and `split_plan_id` + metric emissions (sam/lucy). 2) console: new panel + heatmap (maria). 3) SDK: opt-in decode + retry helper (cheng). 4) security: review suggestion payload content (ops-bot). 5) rollout plan feature flag + 5% canary (tim).

cheng: I'll open a design doc and link to it here. For now we should capture sample wire format for the header and minimal JSON body. Example header value (base64 of JSON): `eyJzdWdnZXN0ZWRfc3BsaXRfcGxhbiI6W3siY291bnQiOjIsImRpbXMiOjUxMn0seyJjb3VudCI6NiwiZGltcyI6MTAyNH1dLCJlc3RfbWl0IjoxODV9` which decodes to `{"suggested_split_plan":[{"count":2,"dims":512},{"count":6,"dims":1024}],"est_unit":185}`

sam: Nice. Please include a short flag in the header to indicate whether the plan is sampled or deterministic: `X-Embed-Split-Plan: sampled=true;id=sp-12345;v=1`.

maria: I'll sketch the console mock tomorrow. If everyone agrees, we can kick off runtime PR next week.

cheng: Sounds good. Any objections to the approach itself?

lucy: No objections. Just watch CPU cost and default opt-out for tenants with strict budgets.

tim: No objections. We'll coordinate the rollout stages with the billing and SRE teams.

ops-bot: Security review queued. ETA 3 business days.

cheng: Great — closing this thread. I'll post the design doc link when ready. :thumbsup:
